title: Single-cell Kcnk5b dose model: passive K+ leak hyperpolarises; Na-channel recruitment gives a small depolarisation inside the physiological window
evidence_kind: SIMULATED with ASSUMED generic parameters; a sign test, not a calibrated model

model.name: SciPy LSODA pump-leak ODE (GHK leaks, Kir, persistent Na, Na/K-ATPase)
model.context: Kcnk5b 0-32x step from the 1x state, read at 10 min, 1 h, 6 h, 24 h; passive (c=0) vs Na-recruitment (g_NaP ~ fold^c) arms. Targets from Yi et al. 2024 PLoS Biol (PMID 38527087).

numerical_checks.name: passive arm, Kcnk5b x8, Vm at 10 min / 1 h
Na-recruitment arm (c=1), Kcnk5b x8, Vm at 1 h; K_i at 6 h
Kcnj13 0-2x at baseline
numerical_checks.result: no Vm change (Kir rectified off at about -32 mV)

numerical_checks.name: CORRECTION: largest fold at which each arm is still physiological at 10 min
numerical_checks.result: c=0.0 fold 32, Vm -86.0 mV (-53.8 from baseline), Na_i 8.1 mM, K_i 120.5 mM; c=1.0 fold 4, Vm -26.2 mV (+6.0 from baseline), Na_i 23.4 mM, K_i 106.9 mM. Screened against Na_i 5-30 mM and K_i 100-150 mM.

numerical_checks.name: what that leaves of the sign test
numerical_checks.result: Inside the window where the cell's ion concentrations stay physiological, the two arms still move Vm in OPPOSITE directions, but the depolarisation is small. At the largest in-range fold the recruitment arm depolarises by only a few mV with a modest K+ loss, while the passive arm hyperpolarises by tens of mV. The larger depolarisation quoted earlier (to about -19 mV) came from 8x fold at 1 h, where Na_i has run to about 90 mM and K_i to about 42 mM: that is a failing cell, not a phenotype, and is withdrawn.

numerical_checks.name: steady state?
numerical_checks.result: no arm is at steady state at any stored time: the per-point Vm change is non-zero throughout, so these are transients

parameter_unknowns: Every conductance, pump capacity and concentration is assumed.
Fixed cell volume; no osmotic regulation.

The recruitment arm scales an inward Na+ conductance by the same factor as the K+ conductance, so recovering a depolarisation is close to built in: it shows a depolarising route is not excluded, not that it is the one used.
Beyond 4x fold the recruitment arm leaves the physiological ion range within 10 min and its later points describe a failing cell.
open_questions: Do hsp70:kcnk5b fin-bud cells show rising Na_i (recruitment) or falling Na_i (passive)?
Does the depolarisation survive Na+-free (NMDG+) extracellular solution? Recruitment requires that it does NOT; that is the falsifying test.
limitations: Ion steady state takes days; only the step-response window is physiologically relevant.
does_not_establish: any zebrafish membrane potential value (parameters are generic)
the Kcnk5b -> Na-channel link itself (it is assumed in the c=1 arm)
